verses.text: The terror of a king is like the roar of a lion; whoever provokes him forfeits his own life.

verses.text: It is honorable for a man to resolve a dispute, but any fool will quarrel.

xrefs.text: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.
To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.
A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.
A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man promotes folly.
Be kind and tenderhearted to one another, forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you.

verses.text: The slacker does not plow in season; at harvest time he looks, but nothing is there.

xrefs.text: Idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth.
Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.
The slacker craves yet has nothing, but the soul of the diligent is fully satisfied.
Finally, the servant who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew that you are a hard man, reaping where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered seed.

verses.text: The intentions of a man’s heart are deep waters, but a man of understanding draws them out.

xrefs.text: The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.
For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.
They devise injustice and say, “We have perfected a secret plan.” For the inner man and the heart are mysterious.

verses.text: The righteous man walks with integrity; blessed are his children after him.

xrefs.text: His descendants will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
They are ever generous and quick to lend, and their children are a blessing.
I will give them one heart and one way, so that they will always fear Me for their own good and for the good of their children after them.

For this is our boast: Our conscience testifies that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and especially in relation to you, in the holiness and sincerity that are from God— not in worldly wisdom, but in the grace of God.
This promise belongs to you and your children and to all who are far off— to all whom the Lord our God will call to Himself.

verses.text: A king who sits on a throne to judge sifts out all evil with his eyes.

xrefs.text: Remove the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
A wise king separates out the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.
A king who judges the poor with fairness— his throne will be established forever.
The mighty King loves justice. You have established equity; You have exercised justice and righteousness in Jacob.
For surely Your enemies, O LORD, surely Your enemies will perish; all evildoers will be scattered.

verses.text: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin”?

xrefs.text: Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
When they sin against You— for there is no one who does not sin— and You become angry with them and deliver them to an enemy who takes them as captives to his own land, whether far or near,
Who can bring out clean from unclean? No one!
What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?

verses.text: Differing weights and unequal measures both are detestable to the LORD.

xrefs.text: Unequal weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are no good.
Dishonest scales are an abomination to the LORD, but an accurate weight is His delight.
You shall not have two differing weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
Can I forget any longer, O house of the wicked, the treasures of wickedness and the short ephah, which is accursed?
You must not use dishonest measures of length, weight, or volume.

verses.text: Even a young man is known by his actions— whether his conduct is pure and upright.

xrefs.text: By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.
The way of a guilty man is crooked, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.
Finally, after three days they found Him in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
The wicked are estranged from the womb; the liars go astray from birth.

verses.text: Ears that hear and eyes that see— the LORD has made them both.

verses.text: Do not love sleep, or you will grow poor; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of food.

xrefs.text: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.
Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.
The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies lacks judgment.

verses.text: There is an abundance of gold and rubies, but lips of knowledge are a rare treasure.

xrefs.text: For wisdom is more precious than rubies, and nothing you desire compares with her.
Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man’s rebuke to a listening ear.
How much better to acquire wisdom than gold! To gain understanding is more desirable than silver.
Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but not so the hearts of fools.

verses.text: Take the garment of the one who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.

xrefs.text: Take the garment of him who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.

Do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts.
He who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer, but the one who hates indebtedness is secure.

verses.text: Food gained by fraud is sweet to a man, but later his mouth is full of gravel.

xrefs.text: Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.

verses.text: Set plans by consultation, and wage war under sound guidance.

xrefs.text: Or what king on his way to war with another king will not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
Only with sound guidance should you wage war, and victory lies in a multitude of counselors.
Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.
After the death of Joshua, the Israelites inquired of the LORD, “Who will be the first to go up and fight for us against the Canaanites?”
For lack of guidance, a nation falls, but with many counselors comes deliverance.

verses.text: He who reveals secrets is a constant gossip; avoid the one who babbles with his lips.

xrefs.text: A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.
He who guards his mouth protects his life, but the one who opens his lips invites his own ruin.
The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.
For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.
You must not go about spreading slander among your people. You must not endanger the life of your neighbor. I am the LORD.

verses.text: Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.

xrefs.text: Anyone who curses his father or mother must surely be put to death.
There is a generation of those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.
As for the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother, may the ravens of the valley pluck it out and young vultures devour it.
For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
They are wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame; wandering stars, for whom blackest darkness has been reserved forever.

verses.text: An inheritance gained quickly will not be blessed in the end.

xrefs.text: Those who want to be rich, however, fall into temptation and become ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires that plunge them into ruin and destruction.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.
He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.
Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay,
Will not all of these take up a taunt against him, speaking with mockery and derision: ‘Woe to him who amasses what is not his and makes himself rich with many loans! How long will this go on?’

verses.text: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.

xrefs.text: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
Make sure that no one repays evil for evil. Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people.
Do not say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”
If anyone returns evil for good, evil will never leave his house.
Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.

verses.text: Unequal weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are no good.

You must use honest scales, a just ephah, and a just bath.

verses.text: A man’s steps are from the LORD, so how can anyone understand his own way?

xrefs.text: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.
I know, O LORD, that a man’s way is not his own; no one who walks directs his own steps.
Who is the man who fears the LORD? He will instruct him in the path chosen for him.
The steps of a man are ordered by the LORD who takes delight in his journey.
Show me Your ways, O LORD; teach me Your paths.

verses.text: It is a trap for a man to dedicate something rashly, only later to reconsider his vows.

xrefs.text: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because He takes no pleasure in fools. Fulfill your vow.
Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill your vows to the Lord.’
If he vows an animal that may be brought as an offering to the LORD, any such animal given to the LORD shall be holy.
If a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised.
Will a man rob God? Yet you are robbing Me! But you ask, ‘How do we rob You?’ In tithes and offerings.

verses.text: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD, searching out his inmost being.

verses.text: Loving devotion and faithfulness preserve a king; by these he maintains his throne.

xrefs.text: Wicked behavior is detestable for kings, for a throne is established through righteousness.

A Psalm of David. I will sing of Your loving devotion and justice; to You, O LORD, I will sing praises.

verses.text: The glory of young men is their strength, and gray hair is the splendor of the old.

xrefs.text: I have written to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.
You are to rise in the presence of the elderly, honor the aged, and fear your God. I am the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: “Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor the strong man in his strength, nor the wealthy man in his riches.

verses.text: Lashes and wounds scour evil, and beatings cleanse the inmost parts.

xrefs.text: Our fathers disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our good, so that we may share in His holiness.
Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; rebuke the discerning man, and he will gain knowledge.
But He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed.

Therefore Jacob’s guilt will be atoned for, and the full fruit of the removal of his sin will be this: When he makes all the altar stones like crushed bits of chalk, no Asherah poles or incense altars will remain standing.
